topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section introduces the lecturer, sets out the lecture series framing, and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the balance between intrinsic replicative errors, inherited genetics, and external exposures through epidemiological and public perspectives.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens contribute to malignant transformation, illustrated in detail by the discovery and mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Activation and DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how environmental chemicals, dietary toxins, and radiation undergo xenobiotic metabolism to form mutagenic DNA adducts and lesions.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the role of non-mutagenic tumour promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental tissue stages in driving cancer outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Demonstrating Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo models, and in vitro assays used to evaluate carcinogenic potential and risk.
